name: Whole-House Renovation Timeline: What to Expect from Discovery to Final Sign-Off

step.name: Step 1: Discovery and existing condition assessment
step.text: During this initial 2 to 4 week stage, you meet with your remodeling contractor to evaluate existing room configurations, structural elements, and mechanical systems. You discuss functional goals, architectural styles, and budget parameters while documenting current framing and utility locations.

step.name: Step 2: Design development and material specifications
step.text: Over the next 6 to 12 weeks, the team creates detailed floor plans, electrical layouts, and finish schedules. You finalize selections for cabinetry, plumbing fixtures, countertops, and flooring so technical construction drawings reflect exact dimensions.

step.name: Step 3: Permit application and municipal review
step.text: Your contractor submits engineering drawings and architectural plans to the local building department for code review. This process typically takes 3 to 8 weeks depending on local agency workloads, and construction cannot begin until official permits are issued.

step.name: Step 4: Demolition, framing, and mechanical rough-ins
step.text: With approvals in hand, crews strip away outdated finishes and reconfigure structural walls over several weeks. Plumbers, electricians, and HVAC technicians then install new rough-in piping, ductwork, and wiring before mandatory municipal rough-in inspections take place.

step.name: Step 5: Drywall, interior finishes, and final punch list
step.text: Once rough-ins pass inspection, insulation and drywall are hung, taped, and finished. Cabinetry, trim, tile, and flooring are installed, followed by final paint, light fixtures, and plumbing trim. A thorough punch list walkthrough resolves minor details before final municipal sign-off.
